summary.text: Squires said AI cannot be excluded from discussions about the future of intellectual property and described IP protection in AI and other emerging fields as a national-security function. He described the USPTO's new Emerging Technologies Office in San Francisco as a hub to advance AI use, engage industry, and help U.S. companies enter federal markets and export AI products. In March 2026 remarks, he described USPTO AI initiatives in patent examination, including an AI-generated prior-art pilot, AI agents to assist examiners on eligibility issues with a human in the loop, and AI tools used to identify fraudulent filings.

statements.text: We just opened an Emerging Technologies Office in San Francisco as part of the agency’s efforts to advance the use of AI and engage with the AI industry. This office serves as a hub to convene our stakeholders involved in AI, enabling them to work with federal officials on how best to steer AI adoption for American dominance. It will help U.S. companies gain a foothold in the federal marketplace and assist them in exporting their AI products and systems to other countries.
